summary: A last source check corrected a sentence I had repeated in two knowledge entries, and the correction strengthens the finding. I had written that the existing runtime test only asserts a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix; re-reading the suite shows two of its scenarios assert the value at the returned index — one refills an index after a lost entry and asserts the index holds the refill (message: 'confirming the original was lost'), and another asserts each returned index holds the entry submitted to it (message: 'wrong-index assignment — indices are 1-based') — while only the simpler scenarios assert a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix. So the repository encodes the expectation I had been attributing to the documentation and example alone: the returned index is expected to hold the caller's entry. I revised both entries with the accurate reading and registered the two test expectations as sources; no conclusion changed, and no execution was requested (validation reports the update valid with execution_requested false). That closes this run's record: three asserted defects with complete comparison chains — the arm-order false success with its measured tick band, the shifted index with its six-configuration condition, and the core trim path unable to compact when the largest node id exceeds the node count — two bounded negatives on out-of-order delivery and on duplication with stale-leader replay, one suspicion that was corrected rather than kept, and the sourced rules behind each condition.
